title: About
text:
The Dashboard is currently a snapshot of data from the SWC/GCNU Neuroinformatics Unit Repositories. All the metrics are based on the Last Updated Date reflected on the top of the dashboard.



Contributors: Contributor is an individual that can read and write to the current repository. Metric calculates the current number of Contributors.
Watchers: The number of users who are tracking a particular repository, receiving notifications regarding its activity.
Open Issues: Issues are tickets that represent bugs or new features that other people report and can collaborate on. Open issues are total of unresolved issues.
Open PRs: A pull request is a request to make a change to the files of the project (code, documentation, README changes, etc.). Open PRs are the total of pull requests with status Open.
Merged PRs: A total of Pull Requests that are accepted into the code base of the project.
Forks: A fork is a copy of the current repository belonging to another user. Forks is how many times the repository has been copied.
Open Issues Median Age: Median number of days for all issues with Open status. If the issue age is zero (meaning there are no open issues), we display “N/A”.
Closed Issues Median Age: Median number of days for all issues with Closed status. If the issue age is zero (meaning there are no closed issues), we display “N/A”.
Issues Response Median Age: Median response time of issues that has a response. If the issue response age is zero (meaning there are no comments), we display “N/A”. If the first response is by the creator of the issue the comment is not counted.
Issues Response Average Age: Average response time of issues that has a response. If the issue response age is zero (meaning there are no comments), we display “N/A”. If the first response is by the creator of the issue the comment is not counted. Calculation is Issues Total Response Time divide by Total Issues



The Atlas usage page tracks how the public BrainGlobe atlas data is downloaded, based on the atlas bucket’s S3 server access logs.
Requests: A successful download of an atlas file (an HTTP GET that returned the file’s contents). Requests aren’t a 1:1 proxy for “an atlas was downloaded” - large atlases are split into many chunk files, each counted separately, so larger atlases may lead to more requests regardless of how many people actually used them.
Atlas downloads: Fetches of an atlas’s manifest.json. The BrainGlobe Atlas API always downloads this file first, once per local install of an atlas, and its path carries the atlas’s canonical name - so it is the source of truth for which atlas was downloaded, and how often. The per-atlas table and chart use this count. Different resolutions of one atlas are counted together. The internal example_mouse test atlas is excluded.
Atlas downloads are also the second metric in the country and client-tool charts, so their totals match the per-atlas total.
Data served: Total data transferred, in GB or TB.
Resource type: Which part of an atlas a request was for - the annotation volume, a per-region mesh, a reference/template image, a terminology, a coordinate space, an atlas’s own manifest, or a neuroglancer state file. Atlas popularity is counted from atlas manifest fetches (see Atlas downloads), not annotation requests - not every use of an atlas reads its annotation.
Client tool: The software inferred to have made a request (e.g. brainglobe-atlasapi, neuroglancer, Pinpoint, a browser, or a custom script), based on the request’s Referer and User-Agent headers. This is an inference, not a verified identity: it assumes any request made with the same underlying library the Atlas API uses (s3fs/boto3) came from the Atlas API, so an unrelated script using that library directly would be misattributed to it.
Country: Geolocated from the requester’s IP address. Requests from IPs that can’t be resolved to a country are counted separately rather than dropped or misattributed.
